text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- An exclusive report by the paper finds that about 7,000 kgs of gold was bought from Nazi Germany by Sweden but the Swedish government during World War Two put pressure on the country's central bank not to ask too many questions about the origins of the gold.

- Head of the Liberal party's parliamentary group, Lars Leijonborg, is seen as the most likely candidate to take over from party leader Maria Leissner who resigned on Monday. She said her reason for resigning after two years was the party's poor ratings in the opinion polls and not getting any respect.

- The American managing director of drugs group Pharmacia & Upjohn causes jitters in the company by his surprise resignation. Analysts said worries over the performance of the merger company reemerged in the market.

- Saab AB and its cooperation partner British Aerospace will on Tuesday and Wednesday meet representatives from the Hungarian government in a bid to sell the Jas 39 Gripen fighter aircraft. The discussions are the follow-up of an agreement in September 1995 by Peter Wallenberg and Hungarian premier Gyula Horn.

- The German and French initiative on Monday to lead the way toward increased integration of the European Union led to uncertainty in the Swedish government, according to the paper. Thus far, the Swedish government has called for a right for EU members to veto issues they dislike, but the foreign minister Lena Hjelm-Wallen on Monday indicated that the government might back down.

- Shares in Swedish-U.S. pharmaceutical company Pharmacia & Upjohn dropped when its chief executive resigned on Monday. The company's chairman Jan Ekberg will take his place temporarily, while board member Richard Brown will step in as chairman until a permanent solution has been found.
- Sweden should increase the wage gap, decentralise wage negotiations and focus on education, according to a report done by four foreign economists for the association SNS.

- Pharmacia & Upjohn board chairman Jan Ekberg said he knew nothing about the unexpected resignation on Monday of Swedish/U.S. group Pharmacia & Upjohn's president and chief executive John Zabriskie until a board meeting on Sunday. Shares plunged as much as 16 crowns on the Stockholm bourse but regained some lost ground in the afternoon. Zabriskie resigned for personal reasons, the company said. - Swedish metals, mining and rubber company Trelleborg said its mining division Boliden will form a joint venture metals prospecting company with Vancouver, Canada-based South Atlantic Resources Ltd owned by Swedish oil and minerals magnate Adolf Lundin. The new company, North Atlantic Natural Resources AB, will be listed on the Stockholm stock exchange in spring with a new share issue over 100 million crown.

- Chairman of Sweden's Liberal party Maria Leissner announced on Monday that she is to resign, citing her failure to boost the party's standing in the opinion polls during her two years as leader as the reason. The most likely successor is Lars Leijonborg, 47, currently head of the Liberal's parliamentary group.
